title: Regular Weyl systems, projective symmetry and massive particles

items.title: Finite canonical representation interface
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\in\mathbb N_0$, let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $2n$, and let $\omega:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be bilinear and alternating, meaning $\omega(v,v)=0$ for every $v\in V$, and nondegenerate, meaning that $\omega(v,w)=0$ for every $w\in V$ implies $v=0$. Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A unitary operator on $\mathcal H$ means a bijective complex-linear isometry. Suppose $W:V\to U(\mathcal H)$ satisfies $W(0)=I$ and

$$W(v)W(w)=e^{-i\lambda\omega(v,w)/2}W(v+w)\qquad(v,w\in V),$$

is regular in the sense that $t\mapsto W(tv)\xi$ is norm-continuous for every $v\in V$ and $\xi\in\mathcal H$, and is irreducible in the sense that its only closed subspaces $M\subseteq\mathcal H$ satisfying $W(v)M\subseteq M$ for every $v\in V$ are $\{0\}$ and $\mathcal H$. Choose a symplectic basis identifying $(V,\omega)$ with $\mathbb R^n\oplus\mathbb R^n$ and $\omega((q,p),(q',p'))=q\cdot p'-p\cdot q'$. Then $W$ is unitarily equivalent, meaning that there is a unitary map $U:\mathcal H\to L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ intertwining the two Weyl actions, to the Schrödinger system

$$\bigl(W_\lambda(q,p)f\bigr)(x)=e^{i\lambda p\cdot(x-q/2)}f(x-q)$$

on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$. Consequently, there is exactly one unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible regular Weyl systems with this fixed finite-dimensional phase space and parameter. No conclusion is asserted for infinite-dimensional phase spaces, nonregular systems, or zero central parameter.
items.proof_route: Apply the current imported finite-dimensional Stone–von Neumann theorem with its actual AC, finite-phase-space, regularity, irreducibility, and nonzero-parameter hypotheses; compose intertwiners for uniqueness.

references.title: Roland Speicher, Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Mechanics, Lecture Notes, Chapter VIII, pp. 43–47
Amritanshu Prasad, An Easy Proof of the Stone-von Neumann-Mackey Theorem, §4.3, pp. 5–10

items.title: Mass cocycle for translations and boosts
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $m>0$ and $\hbar>0$ be real parameters. Let $dx$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^d$. For $z\in\mathbb C$, write $e^z:=\exp z:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}z^k/k!$ for the complex exponential, whose series converges for every $z$. Let $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^d,dx;\mathbb C)$ be the complex measurable functions with finite $\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f(x)|^2\,dx$, modulo equality almost everywhere with respect to $dx$, with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)\overline{g(x)}\,dx$. For $a,v\in\mathbb R^d$, define the translation and modulation operators

$$T(a)f(x)=f(x-a),\qquad B_m(v)f(x)=e^{imv\cdot x/\hbar}f(x).$$

These are unitary operators and satisfy

$$B_m(v)T(a)=e^{imv\cdot a/\hbar}T(a)B_m(v),\qquad B_m(v)T(a)B_m(v)^*T(a)^*=e^{imv\cdot a/\hbar}I.$$

Writing $p=mv$, the associated Weyl operators are

$$W(a,p)f(x)=e^{ip\cdot(x-a/2)/\hbar}f(x-a).$$

They form the canonical regular system on $V=\mathbb R^d\oplus\mathbb R^d$ with $\omega((a,p),(a',p'))=a\cdot p'-p\cdot a'$ and parameter $\lambda=1/\hbar$, meaning $W(0)=I$ and $W(\xi)W(\eta)=e^{-i\omega(\xi,\eta)/(2\hbar)}W(\xi+\eta)$. This system is strongly continuous on every line and has no nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. Every map $\widetilde W:V\to U(K)$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space $K$ with this same multiplication law, strong continuity on every line, and irreducibility is unitarily equivalent to it, meaning a unitary intertwiner exists.

Define $G_d=\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$ with the product Euclidean topology and multiplication

$$ (a,v,\theta)(a',v',\theta')=(a+a',v+v',\theta+\theta'-v'\cdot a). $$

Let $Z=\{(0,0,\theta):\theta\in\mathbb R\}$. The maps $\Pi_m(a,v,\theta)=e^{im\theta/\hbar}B_m(v)T(a)$ form a strongly continuous unitary representation of this topological group, and $Z$ acts by the scalar character $\chi_m(\theta)=e^{im\theta/\hbar}$. For every finite $r\ge1$ and pairwise distinct $m_1,\dots,m_r>0$, the direct sum of these representations has pairwise distinct central characters $\chi_{m_j}$. These are mathematical representation statements for formal parameters; no measured mass, action constant, or physical superselection law is asserted.
items.proof_route: Prove translations and modulations unitary, derive their exact commutator and central-extension group law, establish strong continuity on a dense smooth core and extend by unitarity, distinguish central characters, then apply finite Weyl uniqueness.

references.title: Domenico Giulini, On Galilei Invariance in Quantum Mechanics and the Bargmann Superselection Rule, §1, pp. 3–8
Amritanshu Prasad, An Easy Proof of the Stone-von Neumann-Mackey Theorem, §4.3, pp. 5–10
Roland Speicher, Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Mechanics, Lecture Notes, Chapter VIII, pp. 43–47

items.title: Spin rotations and projective $SO(3)$
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $SU(2)=\{W\in M_2(\mathbb C):W^*W=I,\det W=1\}$, and let $\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. For $i\in\{x,y,z\}$ put $A_i(t)=\cos(t/2)I-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_i$. Give $SU(2)$ its standard smooth matrix-manifold structure and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ its finite-dimensional operator-norm topology. Let $V\ne\{0\}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $D:SU(2)\to U(V)$ be a group homomorphism whose matrix-valued map into $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ is continuously differentiable; this specifies the regularity meant here by a differentiable unitary representation. Define its self-adjoint infinitesimal generators $J_i$ by $\frac{d}{dt}D(A_i(t))|_{t=0}=-iJ_i$. For complex-linear maps $X,Y:V\to V$, write $[X,Y]:=XY-YX$. Assume $[J_x,J_y]=iJ_z$, $[J_y,J_z]=iJ_x$, and $[J_z,J_x]=iJ_y$, and that the triple is irreducible, meaning that no nonzero proper subspace $M\subset V$ satisfies $J_iM\subseteq M$ for all $i$. The spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$ is its largest $J_z$ eigenvalue, as in the finite spin-block classification. Then

$$D(-I)=(-1)^{2s}I_V.$$

Let $\rho:SU(2)\to SO(3)$ be the standard two-sheeted covering homomorphism with kernel $\{I,-I\}$. Give $PU(V)=U(V)/\{zI:|z|=1\}$ its quotient topology and let $q:U(V)\to PU(V)$ be the quotient map; write $[U]:=q(U)$. The ray action $R\mapsto[D(W)]$ for any lift $W$ of $R$ is a well-defined continuous homomorphism $SO(3)\to PU(V)$. For integer $s$, $D$ itself descends to an ordinary unitary representation of $SO(3)$; for half-integer $s$, its unitary representation does not descend, while its ray representation does. No classification of all projective representations of $SO(3)$ is asserted.

The projective descent is summarized by the following commutative diagram; $q$ is the quotient map $U(V)\to PU(V)$ and $\overline D$ is the ray representation just defined.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}
SU(2) \arrow[r,"D"] \arrow[d,"\rho"'] & U(V) \arrow[d,"q"]\\
SO(3) \arrow[r,"\overline D"'] & PU(V)
\end{tikzcd}
```

The proof below verifies that $q\circ D$ is constant on each $\rho$-fiber, which defines $\overline D$ and makes this diagram commute; no proof step relies on the diagram.
items.proof_route: Identify the 2π z-rotation with −I, exponentiate its finite self-adjoint generator, evaluate on the spin-s weight basis supplied by the current finite spin-block theorem, then descend through the two-sheeted cover.

references.title: Peter Bongaarts, Quantum Theory: A Mathematical Approach, Chapter 24, §24.8.1–§24.8.5, pp. 385–388
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 7, §7.1, pp. 141–152
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9, §2, pp. 11–18

items.title: Sector restriction as observable algebra
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{j=1}^r\mathcal H_j$ be a finite orthogonal direct sum of nonzero complex Hilbert spaces, with $r\ge1$, and let $P_j$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_j$. Write $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ for the algebra of bounded linear operators on $\mathcal H$. Let $\mathcal A$ be the block-diagonal subalgebra

$$\mathcal A=\left\{A\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H):A=\sum_{j=1}^rP_jAP_j\right\}.$$

For every trace-class operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$, define $\mathcal E(\rho)=\sum_{j=1}^rP_j\rho P_j$. Then, for every $A\in\mathcal A$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal E(\rho)A).$$

Thus $\rho$ and $\mathcal E(\rho)$ define the same trace functional on the specified block-diagonal algebra. This is relative to the declared algebra; it implies no universal superselection law for a larger observable algebra.
items.proof_route: Expand the trace over the finitely many orthogonal blocks and use the published bounded-cyclicity lemma to make every off-diagonal block trace vanish; this is algebra-relative, not a universal superselection claim.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, §3.6, trace-class operators and trace cyclicity
Anthony W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Digital Second Edition, Chapter II, §5, pp. 49–52
Domenico Giulini, On Galilei Invariance in Quantum Mechanics and the Bargmann Superselection Rule, §1, pp. 7–8

title: Regular Weyl systems, projective symmetry and massive particles — Examples

items.title: Boost-translation loop phase
items.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. For $z\in\mathbb C$, write $e^z:=\exp z:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}z^k/k!$ for the complex exponential, whose series converges for every $z$. Let $dx$ be Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^d$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $m>0$ and $\hbar>0$, and take $a,v\in\mathbb R^d$. Put $\theta=mv\cdot a/\hbar$ and let $T(a)f(x)=f(x-a)$ and $B_m(v)f(x)=e^{imv\cdot x/\hbar}f(x)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d,dx;\mathbb C)$. Their loop $B_m(v)T(a)B_m(v)^*T(a)^*$ equals $e^{i\theta}I$, so a common scalar phase leaves squared overlap unchanged on an isolated component. In the explicitly defined two-arm path model below, applying the loop to exactly one arm gives recombination squared overlap $\cos^2(\theta/2)$, while applying the same scalar to both arms gives squared overlap $1$.
items.proof_route: Use the exact cocycle for the loop; define a two-dimensional arm space and one-arm phase gate, then compute the output overlap and compare it with a common global phase.

references.title: Domenico Giulini, On Galilei Invariance in Quantum Mechanics and the Bargmann Superselection Rule, §1, pp. 3–8

items.title: Finite matrices cannot satisfy exact canonical commutation relations
items.statement: For every positive integer $d$ and every $\hbar>0$, there exist matrices $Q,P\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ such that $QP-PQ=i\hbar I_d$.
items.proof_route: Define the finite matrix trace and expand tr(QP) and tr(PQ) as finite sums; reindex one sum and use commutativity of complex multiplication to get a contradiction.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Digital Second Edition, Chapter II, §5, trace-class definitions and cyclicity exercise, pp. 49–52 (the proof here is the explicit finite sum)
